Retrieve CDISC implementation-guide variable metadata

Source: R/get_ig.R
get_ig.Rd

Mirrors get_ct, but for implementation-guide (IG) variable metadata rather than controlled terminology. Unlike CT, which uses a single validity-date timeline per standard, ig_sdtm bundles two independently-versioned sources (the SDTM Model and the SDTMIG; see ig_sdtm), so there is no single "latest" snapshot to default to: version = NULL returns every source and version, for the caller to filter further (by source/domain/class for ig_sdtm, or dataset/category for ig_adam). build_domain_spec does this filtering for the PP, SUPPPP, and ADPP datasets specifically.

Usage

get_ig(standard = c("sdtm", "adam"), version = NULL)

Arguments

standard

One of "sdtm" or "adam".

version

A version string present in the version column (e.g. "3.2" for SDTMIG, "1.7" for the SDTM Model, "1.2" for ADaMIG). NULL (the default) returns all versions.

Value

A data frame: ig_sdtm or ig_adam, optionally filtered to one version.

Details

SDTMIG coverage. The SDTMIG PP domain and the generic SUPP– structure are only available at version 3.2, because that is as far as the Rsdtm source this package copies from goes (see data-raw/ig_source/README.md); no newer SDTMIG's PP/SUPP– tables were available to source. As a result, PP variables CDISC added or renamed after SDTMIG 3.2 are absent from ig_sdtm - notably PPANMETH, EPOCH, and PTAETORD (added later), and the PPDTC to PPPDTC rename (SDTMIG 3.2 still has PPDTC). Sourcing a newer SDTMIG - via a CDISC Library API key or a newer public transcription - would close this gap.

get_ig("sdtm")

#>                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   notes
#> 1                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Short character value for --TEST used as a column name when\nconverting a dataset from a vertical format to a horizontal\nformat. The short value can be up to 8 characters. Examples:\nPLAT, SYSBP, RRMIN, EYEEXAM.
#> 2                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     Long name For --TESTCD. Examples: Platelet, Systolic Blood\nPressure, Summary (Min) RR Duration, Eye Examination.
#> 3                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      If the value of --ORRES is modified for coding purposes, then\nthe modified text is placed here.
#> 4                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Further description of --TESTCD and --TEST. Example: “The\npercentage of cells with +1 intensity of staining” when\nMITESTCD = TTF1.
#> 5                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Used to define a category of topic-variable values. Examples:\nHEMATOLOGY, URINALYSIS, CHEMISTRY, HAMILTON\nDEPRESSION SCALE, SF36, MICRO ARRAY, EGFR\nMUTATION ANALYSIS
#> 6                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Used to define a further categorization of --CAT values.\nExample: DIFFERENTIAL.
#> 7                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Position of the subject during a measurement or examination.\nExamples: SUPINE, STANDING, SITTING.
#> 8                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Body System or Organ Class that is involved for a finding from\nthe standard hierarchy for dictionary-coded results. Example:\nMedDRA SOC.
#> 9                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Result of the measurement or finding as originally received or\ncollected. Examples: 120, <1, POS.
#> 10                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Unit for --ORRES. Examples: IN, LB, kg/L.
#> 11                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         Lower end of normal range or reference range for results stored\nin --ORRES.
#> 12                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         Upper end of normal range or reference range for results stored\nin --ORRES.
#> 13  Contains the result value for all findings, copied or derived from\n--ORRES in a standard format or in standard units. --STRESC\nshould store all results or findings in character format; if results\nare numeric, they should also be stored in numeric format in --\nSTRESN. For example, if various tests have results “NONE”,\n“NEG”, and “NEGATIVE” in --ORRES and these results\neffectively have the same meaning, they could be represented in\nstandard format in --STRESC as "NEGATIVE".
#> 14                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         Used for continuous or numeric results or findings in standard\nformat; copied in numeric format from --STRESC. --STRESN\nshould store all numeric test results or findings.
#> 15                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Standardized units used for --STRESC and --STRESN.\nExample: mol/L.
#> 16                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     Lower end of normal range or reference range for standardized\nresults (e.g., --STRESC, --STRESN) represented in\nstandardized units (--STRESU).
#> 17                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     Upper end of normal range or reference range for standardized\nresults (e.g., --STRESC, --STRESN) represented in\nstandardized units (--STRESU).
#> 18                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     Normal range or reference range for results stored in --STRESC\nthat are character in ordinal or categorical scale. Example:\nNegative to Trace.
#> 19                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Used to indicate the value is outside the normal range or\nreference range. May be defined by --ORNRLO and --ORNRHI\nor other objective criteria. Examples: Y, N; HIGH, LOW;\nNORMAL; ABNORMAL.
#> 20                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             Used to categorize the result of a finding. Example:\nMALIGNANT or BENIGN for tumor findings. RESISTANCE\nVARIANT for genetic variation.
#> 21                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Used to indicate that a question was not asked or a test was not\ndone, or a test was attempted but did not generate a result.\nShould be null or have a value of NOT DONE.
#> 22                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Reason not done. Used in conjunction with --STAT when value\nis NOT DONE.
#> 23                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Filename for an external file, such as one for an ECG waveform\nor a medical image.
#> 24                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 Name or identifier of the vendor (e.g., laboratory) that provided\nthe test results.
#> 25                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             Logical Observation Identifiers Names and Codes (LOINC)\ncode for the topic variable such as a lab test.
#> 26                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Defines the type of specimen used for a measurement.\nExamples: SERUM, PLASMA, URINE, DNA, RNA.
#> 27                                                                                                                                                                                                                         Defines the specific anatomical or biological region of a tissue,\norgan specimen or the region from which the specimen is\nobtained, as defined in the protocol, such as a section or part of\nwhat is described in the --SPEC variable. Examples: CORTEX,\nMEDULLA, MUCOSA
#> 28                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Defines the condition of the specimen. Example: CLOUDY.
#> 29                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       Describes the usability of the specimen for the test. The value\nwill be N if the specimen is not usable, and null if the specimen\nis usable.
#> 30                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Anatomical location of the subject relevant to the collection of\nthe measurement. Examples: RECTAL for temperature, ARM\nfor blood pressure.
#> 31                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Qualifier for anatomical location or specimen further detailing\nlaterality. Examples: RIGHT, LEFT, BILATERAL
#> 32                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 Qualifier for anatomical location or specimen further detailing\ndirectionality. Examples: ANTERIOR, LOWER, PROXIMAL
#> 33                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Qualifier for anatomical location or specimen further detailing\nthe distribution, which means arrangement of, apportioning of. .\nExamples: ENTIRE, SINGLE, SEGMENT, MANY.
#> 34                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Method of the test or examination. Examples: EIA (Enzyme\nImmunoassay), ELECTROPHORESIS, DIPSTICK
#> 35                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                A unique identifier for a particular run of a test on a particular\nbatch of samples.
#> 36                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Analysis method applied to obtain a summarized result.\nAnalysis method describes the method of secondary processing\napplied to a complex observation result (e.g. an image or a\ngenetic sequence).
#> 37                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Lead or leads identified to capture the measurement for a test\nfrom an instrument. Examples: LEAD I, LEAD V2, LEAD\nCM5.
#> 38                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                The consciousness state of the subject at the time of\nmeasurement. Examples: CONSCIOUS, SEMI-CONSCIOUS,\nUNCONSCIOUS
#> 39                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Indicator used to identify a baseline value. Should be Y or null.
#> 40                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Indicator used to identify fasting status. Valid values include Y,\nN, U or null if not relevant.
#> 41                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Used to indicate a derived record (e.g., a record that represents\nthe average of other records such as a computed baseline).\nShould be Y or null.
#> 42                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           Role of the person who provided the evaluation. Used only for\nresults that are subjective (e.g., assigned by a person or a\ngroup). Examples: ADJUDICATION COMMITTEE,\nINDEPENDENT ASSESSOR, RADIOLOGIST.
#> 43                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Used to distinguish multiple evaluators with the same role\nrecorded in --EVAL. Examples: RADIOLOGIST1 or\nRADIOLOGIST2
#> 44                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    In cases where more than one assessor provides an evaluation of\na result or response, this flag identifies the record that is\nconsidered, by an independent assessor, to be the accepted\nevaluation. Expected to be Y or null.
#> 45                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             Description of toxicity quantified by --TOXGR such as NCI\nCTCAE Short Name. Examples: HYPERCALCEMIA,\nHYPOCALCEMIA. Sponsor should specify which scale and\nversion is used in the Sponsor Comments column of the Define\nXML document.
#> 46                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         Records toxicity grade using a standard toxicity scale (such as\nthe NCI CTCAE). Sponsor should specify which scale and\nversion is used in the Sponsor Comments column of the Define\ndata definition document. Example: 2.
#> 47                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Describes the severity or intensity of a particular finding.\nExamples: MILD, MODERATE, SEVERE.
#> 48                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Describes the relationship of a particular finding to the death of\na subject. Examples: Y, N or U.
#> 49                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Indicates the lower limit of quantitation for an assay. Units will\nbe those used for --STRESU.
#> 50                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Indicates the upper limit of quantitation for an assay. Units will\nbe those used for --STRESU.
#> 51                                                                                                                                                                              Indicates whether the values in the result variables for this\nrecord should be excluded from summary statistical calculations\nsuch as Mean, Standard Deviation, and Count (and others).\nExpected to be Y or null. --EXCLFL should not be used when -\n-STAT is NOT DONE. Not to be used with human clinical\ntrials.
#> 52                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 Reason excluded from statistics. Used in conjunction with --\nEXCLFL when its value is Y. Not to be used with human\nclinical trials
#> 53                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 Short character value for --TEST used as a column name when\nconverting a dataset from a vertical format to a horizontal format.\nThe short value can be up to 8 characters. Examples: PLAT,\nSYSBP, RRMIN, EYEEXAM.
#> 54                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Long name For --TESTCD. Examples: Platelet, Systolic Blood\nPressure, Summary (Min) RR Duration, Eye Examination.

Example: "The\npercentage of cells with +1 intensity of staining" when MITEST\n= Thyroid Transcription Factor 1.
#> 57                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Used to define a category of topic-variable values. Examples:\nHEMATOLOGY, URINALYSIS, CHEMISTRY, HAMILTON\nDEPRESSION SCALE, SF36, EGFR MUTATION ANALYSIS.
#> 58                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 Used to define a further categorization of --CAT values.\nExample: WBC DIFFERENTIAL.
#> 59                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   Position of the subject during a measurement or examination.\nExamples: SUPINE, STANDING, SITTING.
#> 60                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           Body System or Organ Class that is involved for a finding from\nthe standard hierarchy for dictionary-coded results. Example:\nMedDRA SOC.
#> 61                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   Result of the measurement or finding as originally received or\ncollected. Examples: 120, <1, POS.
#> 62                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Unit for --ORRES. Examples: in, LB, kg/L.
#> 63                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         Lower end of normal range or reference range for results stored in\n--ORRES.
#> 64                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         Upper end of normal range or reference range for results stored in\n--ORRES.
#> 65                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Reference value for the result or finding as originally received or\ncollected. --ORREF uses the same units as --ORRES, if\napplicable. Examples: value from predicted normal value in\nspirometry tests.
#> 66   Contains the result value for all findings, copied or derived from\n--ORRES in a standard format or in standard units. --STRESC\nshould store all results or findings in character format; if results\nare numeric, they should also be stored in numeric format in\n--STRESN. For example, if various tests have results "NONE",\n"NEG", and "NEGATIVE" in --ORRES and these results\neffectively have the same meaning, they could be represented in\nstandard format in --STRESC as "NEGATIVE".
#> 67                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         Used for continuous or numeric results or findings in standard\nformat; copied in numeric format from --STRESC. --STRESN\nshould store all numeric test results or findings.
#> 68                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Standardized units used for --STRESC and --STRESN. Example:\nmol/L.
#> 69                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Lower end of normal range or reference range for standardized\nresults (e.g., --STRESC, --STRESN) represented in standardized\nunits (-STRESU).
#> 70                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Upper end of normal range or reference range for standardized\nresults (e.g., --STRESC, --STRESN) represented in standardized\nunits (-STRESU).
#> 71                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     Normal range or reference range for results stored in --STRESC\nthat are character in ordinal or categorical scale. Example:\nNegative to Trace.
#> 72                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Reference value for the result or finding copied or derived from\n--ORREF in a standard format.
#> 73                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Reference value for continuous or numeric results or findings in\nstandard format or in standard units. --STREFN uses the same\nunits as --STRESN, if applicable.
#> 74                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Used to indicate the value is outside the normal range or\nreference range. May be defined by --ORNRLO and --ORNRHI\nor other objective criteria. Examples: Y, N; HIGH, LOW;\nNORMAL; ABNORMAL.
#> 75                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             Used to categorize the result of a finding. Example:\nMALIGNANT or BENIGN for tumor findings. RESISTANCE\nVARIANT for genetic variation.
#> 76                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Characterization of the duration of a biological process resulting\nin a particular finding. Examples: ACUTE, CHRONIC,\nSUBACUTE.
#> 77                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             Description of the distribution pattern of a finding within the\nexamined area. Examples: FOCAL, MULTIFOCAL, DIFFUSE,\nFOCAL MULTIFOCAL.
#> 78                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Used to indicate that a question was not asked or a test was not\ndone, or a test was attempted but did not generate a result. Examples: CORTEX,\nMEDULLA, MUCOSA

#> 88                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Qualifier for anatomical location or specimen further detailing\nlaterality. Examples: RIGHT, LEFT, BILATERAL
#> 89                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 Qualifier for anatomical location or specimen further detailing\ndirectionality. #> 91                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Method of the test or examination. #> 92                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                A unique identifier for a particular run of a test on a particular\nbatch of samples.

Examples: CONSCIOUS, SEMI-CONSCIOUS,\nUNCONSCIOUS

Should be Y or null.
#> 98                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Indicator used to identify fasting status. Valid values include Y,\nN, U or null if not relevant.

#> 240                 Short name of the pharmacokinetic parameter. It can be used as a column name when converting a dataset from a vertical to a horizontal format.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               DM.SITEID. SITEID is required in ADSL, but permissible in other datasets.
#> 528                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   Character description of a grouping or pooling of clinical sites for analysis purposes. For example, SITEGR3 is the name of a variable containing site group (pooled site) names, where the grouping has been done according to the third site grouping algorithm, defined in variable metadata; SITEGR3 does not mean the third group of sites.
#> 529                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   Numeric representation of SITEGRy. There must be a one-to-one relationship between SITEGRyN and SITEGRy within a study.\nSITEGRyN cannot be present unless SITEGRy is also present. When SITEGRy and SITEGRyN are present, then on a given record, either both must be populated or both must be null.
#> 530                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Character description of geographical region. For example, REGION1 might have values of "Asia", "Europe", "North America", "Rest of World"; REGION2 might have values of "United States", "Rest of World".
#> 531                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         Numeric representation of REGIONy. Orders REGIONy for analysis and reporting.There must be a one-to-one relationship between REGIONyN and REGIONy within a study.\nREGIONyN cannot be present unless REGIONy is also present. When REGIONy and REGIONyN are present, then on a given record, either both must be populated or both must be null.
#> 532                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       These flags identify whether or not the subject is included in the specified population. A minimum of one subject-level population flag variable is required in ADSL.\nNot all of the indicators listed here need to be included in ADSL. As stated in Section 3.1.4, Flag Variable Conventions, only those indicators corresponding to populations defined in the statistical analysis plan or populations used as a basis for analysis need be included in ADSL.\nThis list of flags is not meant to be all-inclusive. Additional population flags may be added.\nThe values of subject-level population flags cannot be blank. If a flag is used, the corresponding numeric version (*FN, where 0 = No and 1 = Yes) of the population flag can also be included. Please also refer to Section 3.1.4, Flag Variable Conventions.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     STRATAR contains the combination of values of the individual stratification factors used for randomization. The exact format should be determined by the sponsor. This variable is intended for studies that use stratified randomization.\nFor example, ">=50, Treatment experienced, N"
#> 540                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Numeric representation of STRATAR. For example, STRATARN=3 when STRATAR=">=50, Treatment experienced, N". There must be a one-to-one relationship between STRATARN and STRATAR within a study.\nSTRATARN cannot be present unless STRATAR is also present. When STRATAR and STRATARN are present, then on a given record, either both must be populated or both must be null.
#> 541                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               STRATwD is a full text description of the stratification factor "w". This text description will remain constant for all subjects. These descriptive variables are included to quickly and clearly communicate critical study design information as well as to facilitate integration.\nFor example, STRAT3D="Hypertension"
#> 542                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 STRATwR is the subject-level value of the "w'th" stratification factor used for randomization.\nFor example, STRAT3R="N"
#> 543                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         Numeric representation of STRATwR. For example, STRAT3RN=0 when STRAT3R="N". There must be a one-to-one relationship between STRATwRN and STRATwR within a study.\nSTRATwRN cannot be present unless STRATwR is also present. When STRATwR and STRATwRN are present, then on a given record, either both must be populated or both must be null.
#> 544                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        STRATAV contains the entire string value represents the combination of values of the individual stratification factors that should have been used and represents the "as verified" value. The STRATAV variables are based on the source documentation and are determined after randomization. If the values used for the randomization of a given subject were all correct, then STRATAV will equal STRATAR. Otherwise, one or more components of the text string for STRATAR and STRATAV will be different.\nThe exact format should be determined by the sponsor. For example, ">=50, Treatment experienced, Y"
#> 545                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Numeric representation of STRATAV. For example, STRATAVN=4 when STRATVR=">=50, Treatment experienced, Y". There must be a one-to-one relationship between STRATAVN and STRATAV within a study.\nSTRATAVN cannot be present unless STRATAV is also present. When STRATAV and STRATAVN are present, then on a given record, either both must be populated or both must be null.
#> 546                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 STRATwV is the "as verified" subject-level value of the "w'th" stratification factor. If the value based on randomization was correct, then STRATwV will equal STRATwR. For example, STRAT3V="Y"
#> 547                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Numeric representation of STRATwV. For example, STRAT3VN=1 when STRAT3V="Y". There must be a one-to-one relationship between STRATwVN and STRATwV within a study.\nSTRATwVN cannot be present unless STRATwV is also present. When STRATwV and STRATwVN are present, then on a given record, either both must be populated or both must be null.

For example when in period 2 the first pooling algorithm dictates that all doses of Drug A (TR02PG1="All doses of Drug A") are pooled together for comparison to all doses of Drug B (TR02PG1="All doses of Drug B"). Useful when planned treatment sequences (TRTSEQP) are pooled together for analysis according to pooling algorithm y. For example, this might be used in an analysis of an extension study when the analysis is based on what the subject received in the parent study as well as in the extension study.

#> 630                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     Analysis value derivation method. DTYPE is used to denote, and must be populated, when the value of AVAL or AVALC has been imputed or derived differently than the other analysis values within the parameter. DTYPE is required to be populated even if AVAL and AVALC are null on the derived record.\nThree common situations when DTYPE should be populated:\n?      A new row is added within a parameter with the analysis value populated based on other rows within the parameter.\n?      A new row is added within a parameter with the analysis value populated based on a constant value or data from other subjects.\n?      An analysis value (AVAL or AVALC) on an existing record is being replaced with a value based on a pre- specified algorithm.\nDTYPE is used to denote analysis values that are "special cases" within a parameter. For each value of DTYPE, the precise derivation algorithm must be defined in analysis variable metadata, even for DTYPE values in the CDISC Controlled Terminology. The controlled terminology for DTYPE is extensible. See Section 4, Implementation Issues, Standard Solutions, and Examples for examples of the use of DTYPE.\nSome examples of DTYPE values:\n?      LOCF = last observation carried forward.\n?      WOCF = worst observation carried forward.\n?      AVERAGE = average of values.
#> 631                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           A text string identifying a pre-specified criterion within a parameter, for example SYSBP > 90. Required if CRITyFL is present. In some cases, the presence of the text string indicates that the criterion is satisfied on this record and CRITyFL is set to Y, while a null value indicates that the criterion is not satisfied or is not evaluable and is accompanied by a null value in CRITyFL. In other cases, the text string identifies the criterion being evaluated and is populated on every row for the parameter, but whether or not the criterion is satisfied is indicated by the value of the variable CRITyFL. See CRITyFL and CRITyFN.\nRefer to Section 4.7, Identification of Records which Satisfy a Predefined Criterion for Analysis Purposes, for additional discussion of CRITy, CRITyFL and CRITyFN.

For example, the grade of a lab analyte is compared to the baseline grade, with the possible conditions being 0 to 1, 0 to 2, etc. The text string identifies the criterion being evaluated (for example, "Grade increase") and is populated on every row for the parameter; which level of the criterion is satisfied is indicated by the value of the variable MCRITyML (for example "0 to 1", "0 to 2", etc.).\nSee MCRITyML and MCRITyMN below, and refer to Section 4.7, Identification of Records which Satisfy a Predefined Criterion for Analysis Purposes, for additional discussion of MCRITy, MCRITyML, and MCRITyMN.
